item.title: GB men take fourth and must wait for LA28 Olympic spot
item.description: Joe Fraser thinks Great Britain can challenge to be world champions in the men's team event next year [Getty Images] Great Britain narrowly missed out on qualifying for the 2028 Olympic Games at the first attempt as they placed fourth in the men's team final at the Gymnastics World Championships. Only the top three in Rotterdam were assured of early qualification for the Games in Los Angeles in two years' time, with defending champions Japan taking the gold medal ahead of Russia in second and China in third. GB's next chance to qualify will be at the World Championships in Chengdu, China in 2027, where a top-nine finish will secure a place in LA. Courtney Tulloch, Joe Fraser, Jake Jarman, Harry Hepworth and Reuben Ward qualified in second place for the final and finished with a total score of 247.395 on Tuesday. The team were leading the standings after four of the six rotations, but they just fell short of staying in the medal places as Japan, Russia and China all improved in the closing stages. Japan took the step on the podium with a score of 251.928. Fraser told BBC Sport the team feel they are in a good position to challenge for titles in the future. "I think collectively, as a team, we can look at the overall of the team final and know that we are definitely amongst the best in the world, and we can compete with the best in the world," Fraser said. "We were taking Japan right the way to the end, and up until the parallel bars, we were with them. "So we know as long as we can work on our routines from the parallel bars and the high bar, we can really contend to be world champions maybe next year." You can watch coverage of the Gymnastics World Championships, which run until Sunday, 25 October, on BBC Two and BBC iPlayer.

After two disappointing seasons in which, by his own admission, he failed to hit the heights expected, there may be those who had forgotten what he can produce. Being left out of the England squad for the World Cup last summer did not help, but he came into this season telling reporters he was looking forward to a "fresh start" under new manager Enzo Maresca. Up until last weekend, that fresh start had been a slow burner with the low point of being sent off in the derby against Manchester United in September, before he sparked into life by netting against Ipswich on Saturday. That was his first Premier League goal in 10 months and a strike that seems to have opened the floodgates, with the 26-year-old netting a superb hat-trick in the 5-1 hammering of Athens at Etihad Stadium on Tuesday. "I enjoyed that a lot," Foden told TNT Sports. "The lads were great again. We showed determination again. I am a forward so I have to keep scoring and helping the team. It is good for my confidence." Asked if he was returning to his best form, Foden said: "Slowly, but surely. Still got a long way to go, but I am going in the right direction. Scoring along the way definitely helps. "I want to keep working hard and keep being the best I can for the manager and the team." item.title: PSG star hailed as ‘most underrated player of all time’ after Barcelona win
item.description: Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Fabian Ruiz has been hailed as the “most underrated player of all time” after scoring in the Champions League holders’ statement 4-2 victory over Barcelona . Ruiz tapped home PSG’s fourth after the French giants were pegged back twice in their win at the Parc des Princes , first by Xavi Espart before Lamine Yamal produced his latest moment of magic to level in the 79th minute. Vitinha’s strike two minutes later gave PSG the lead once again and it didn’t take much longer for Ruiz to put the game out of sight, finishing Achraf Hakimi ’s cross. “He could be the most underrated player of all time, Fabian Ruiz,” said Joe Cole on TNT Sports . “He’s won everything in the game, Champions League, does his job, and what I would say is they look a stronger side with him in.” Fabian Ruiz scored PSG's fourth goal (AP) Ruiz came into the season off the back of winning the World Cup with Spain, being an integral figure in midfield alongside Rodri . PSG winger Desire Doue, who brilliantly fired in the opener in Paris, was delighted with his side’s performance. “The atmosphere was crazy tonight,” he said. “We did a great job because we won obviously but we’re really happy with the content of the match. “We did some amazing things, we never quit and when you win against one of the biggest teams in Europe you are really happy so we are really happy tonight. I’m always happy when I can help the team. “Every game you say that we send a message, I don’t know. We just try and play the best football we can and we did a great job tonight.” PSG return to action this weekend against Ligue 1 leaders Lyon, who are above them in the table on goal difference.

item.title: Eagles rumors: Hollywood Brown could be next trade domino in Philly’s fire sale
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Eagles rumors: Hollywood Brown could be next trade domino in Philly’s fire sale appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline three weeks away , the Philadelphia Eagles find themselves in a unique spot. After spending years as pretty consistent buyers, with Howie Roseman using future picks for present-day reinforcements to varying results, the Birds have already said goodbye to Cam Jurgens after some early struggles to adapt to Chris Kuper’s system and could end up trading a few more win-now pieces as that prospect becomes less likely with each passing week. One player who could be on the move? Hollywood Brown, with Jordan Schultz of Fox Sports noting on social media that the Eagles could ship out the speedster to an interesting party after failing to find a clear role in Sean Mannion’s offense. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Sources: Eagles WR Marquise ‘Hollywood’ Brown is a name that teams seeking WR help believe could be traded in the coming weeks,” Schultz wrote. “Brown is healthy, has a 1,000-yard season on his resume, and recorded 49 catches for 587 yards and five TDs with the Chiefs last season. He hasn’t had much of an opportunity in Philadelphia.” Initially signing with the Eagles all the way back in March, Hollywood likely saw an impending AJ Brown trade coming in June and assumed he could slide right into a starting role alongside DeVonta Smith. And yet, between the trade for Dontayvion Wicks in April, the trade up to select Makai Lemon in the 2026 NFL Draft, and the emergence of Darius Cooper as a high-upside young wide receiver, Brown has earned just two carries and no targets as a member of the Eagles, even if an ankle injury has only allowed him to appear in just one game in 2026. Would Brown love to be traded? Sure, and if a playoff team comes calling, Roseman would absolutely talk turkey just like he should with almost any other player on the roster, but considering Brown’s recent production, one has to wonder how robust his market will even be. It is for me.” Jensen’s first season at his alma mater was equal parts “struggle” and “learning experience,” as the Runnin’ Utes finished 10-22 and 2-16 in conference play. Much has been said about Utah having fallen far below its past peak — back when Jensen himself was starring for Rick Majerus — and Jensen knew taking the helm of the program would require a daunting turnaround effort, one made even more challenging by Big 12 competition. “Living through where Utah basketball has been and where it is now, the one thing (that stands out from Year 1) is how good the Big 12 is,” Jensen said. “There’s never an easy night off, the coaching is phenomenal. The Big 12 is a gauntlet, and now we know more of what to expect there. “... (College is) a very different brand of basketball (compared to the NBA or Europe), a different cadence. item.title: Matt LaFleur calls out NFL officials over Jordan Love’s treatment after Packers win over the Cowboys
item.description: The Green Bay Packers came away with a 23-13 win over Dallas on Sunday Night Football, but the victory did not stop Matt LaFleur from questioning the referees’ handling of roughing the passer calls. The Packers coach raised concerns about what he saw as inconsistent enforcement of the rule. The Packers have been penalized for roughing the passer six times this season, more than any other NFL team. Three of those flags came against Dak Prescott in the matchup with Dallas, while every other team had no more than four entering the discussion. LaFleur addressed the issue with reporters Monday, emphasizing that officials should apply the roughing the passer rule consistently for all quarterbacks. He feels Jordan Love has not received the same protection, noting that opposing defenders have hit or sacked the Packers quarterback 39 times this season without a single roughing the passer penalty. item.title: Mr. Build-It: Ross Steelman unafraid to forge his own clubs, unparalleled path to PGA Tour
item.description: PONTE VEDRA BEACH, Fla. — Ross Steelman worked in a golf repair shop during the winter in Missouri when he was in high school. He didn’t own a new club until he was 14, instead rummaging through 50-gallon bins for used clubs and making them work. That was the case even this year when he won the Korn Ferry Tour points list . During a month break in the schedule in late spring, Steelman was so frustrated with his driving that he went on eBay and bought a driver shaft, a 3-wood shaft and a hybrid head. He also bought a putter, an old TaylorMade Rossa Daytona, that he used the rest of the season. And he wasn’t done. “Two weeks later, I bought off True Temper’s website a steel fiber graphite iron shaft and put it in an 8-iron and messed around with it on the range at home,” Steelman said. “I took it out on tour and showed the guys this is what I want. They said: ‘This is terrible. It’s too light, it’s no good, you’re going to hate it.’ The swing weight was five weights too light. I said: ‘Perfect. Can you build a set?’” He said his approach statistics improved two shots the rest of the year. He figures it worked in part because “I did it myself so I trust it even more.” But it was how he found it that showed that Steelman isn’t afraid to try anything . He loved the driver shaft he bought on eBay so much that he went on ChatGPT and wrote, “Is there an iron shaft that has a similar feel?” “It was perfect,” Steelman said. “I cut it, glued it, put it in and it felt great. I trust it because it came from me. I swing fast, I hit it a long way, I hit it high. No rep in his right mind would say, ‘I think you should use this graphite shaft in your irons.’” He is the ultimate gear head, developed from his high school days when he worked in a club repair shop in the winter and learned how to build, grind and bend clubs. He got away from it while at Missouri and Georgia Tech, but it never really left him — especially this year. “That’s the romantic part of golf, finding something you’re really excited about and knowing you have a special connection to it because it’s something you found,” he said. “It gets lost as a professional because we can text somebody and it (a club) will show up in two days. That’s never been my path in golf.” Austin Hitt wins KFT finale as 20 players secure 2027 PGA Tour cards Under a persistent rain, on a gloomy day, futures were solidified for a field of 59 in the Korn Ferry Tour season finale. item.title: I know how good Foden is - Maresca
item.description: I know how good Foden is - Maresca Enzo Maresca says he knows exactly how good Phil Foden is, before his hat-trick in our 5-1 UEFA Champions League victory over AEK Athens. Men's Team AEK Athens display massive for my confidence, says Lewis The City forward followed his goal in the win over Ipswich Town with a superb treble as we picked up our second win in Europe this season. It’s been a fabulous return to form after missing a month’s work of action after picking up a red card and three-game suspension in our victory over Manchester United in Old Trafford. Asked if he had returned with an extra fire in his belly, Maresca said the Academy graduate was showing his quality long before the unfortunate ban. “I was very happy with Phil, even before the red card to be honest,” the Italian said in his postmatch news conference. “I said since day one I consider him one of the best English players. “I know how good he is and we are just trying to help him because I’m sure he will help us. “We know Phil is a top player. For different reasons he had some problems in the last two years but I know he is going to help us and how good he is. That’s why I’m keen to have him in the best way.” The pick of his goals was his second, started with a brilliant long pass from Rayan Cherki to pick out Rico Lewis who laid the ball back for Foden to smack home. Cherki also scored a superb goal himself with a dummy that was followed by a perfect low finish. “I think Rayan like the others, had a good game,” Maresca said. “He made an impact in some moments like the goal. “We know we can expect anything from Rayan at any moment.” Asked if he was a potential Ballon d’Or winner of the future, the boss added: “I don’t know, the only thing I can say, this is a team sport not a single sport. “Erling [Haaland] is a top player, so is Rayan and Elliot. We have to think about the 20/25 players that are in the squad.” City v Brighton: £20 for adults and £1 for U18s Tickets are now on sale for our Carabao Cup fourth round meeting with Brighton. item.title: 7 most notable players born after LeBron James' NBA debut, from Cam Boozer to V.J. Edgecombe
item.description: 7 most notable players born after LeBron James' NBA debut, from Cam Boozer to V.J. Edgecombe originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Four different U.S. presidents. Twenty-nine generations of iPhones. A new NBA franchise, with two more on the way. Those are just a few ways the world has changed since the last NBA season without LeBron James on a roster — it's been a long while. James, approaching the quarter-century mark in the league as he embarks on Year 24 on Tuesday night in his 76ers debut, has already set the NBA record for seasons played. As James has set more records and remained an All-NBA-level talent into his 40s, his age has become just as much of a representation of his greatness. item.title: Max Verstappen backs Isack Hadjar to take over Red Bull F1 role
item.description: Motorsport photo Four-time Formula 1 champion Max Verstappen has backed Isack Hadjar to eventually succeed him at Red Bull. Hadjar joined Red Bull alongside Verstappen at the start of 2026 after impressing in his rookie season with sister outfit Racing Bulls . While the Milton Keynes outfit has struggled for some time to find a team-mate for the Dutchman who could extract the same level of performance from the car, Hadjar has impressed so far. With six rounds remaining in the 2026 season, Verstappen sits fourth in the drivers' championship with 221 points, while Hadjar is eighth with 97 points, having missed three race weekends due to a wrist injury. While speaking to Canal+, Verstappen discussed his 22-year-old team-mate. "Isack, he’s still a very young guy. He’s been a part of the Red Bull programme for a while now," Verstappen said. "Even when he was still not racing in Formula 1, he’s been around to some of the races, listening in and following. Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing "So, I slowly start to feel a little bit old having a younger team-mate by quite a few years. But that’s a normal process, and that’s also what, as a team, you should be looking for, right? "I’m not going to race forever, and at one point you need new talent coming into the team to try and take over at one point. That’s always been a little bit the way that Red Bull works, finding new talent, and I think that will continue for a long time. "As a team-mate, he has been great. He’s just getting started, but it has been really nice." When asked if Hadjar could take his role within the team in the future, Verstappen added: "That’s what I hope. As I said, I’m not racing here forever. He has a few years on me, so hopefully he can stay around for a bit longer." To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: ‘Win it all’ – Stephen A Smith has clear favourite to win NBA championship
item.description: Photo by Jason Mendez/Getty Images for SiriusXM Stephen A Smith has revealed his pick to win the 2026/27 NBA Championship – and it’s not the New York Knicks. Smith believes the Oklahoma City Thunder are the team to beat this year and has warned the Knicks of a “tough road ahead”. Speaking ahead of the new season, he said: “October 20th, 2026, the opening of the 2026/27 NBA season, before anything else happens a ring ceremony will take place, it will be placed on the fingers of the New York Knicks, and the banner will raise to the rafters. “Finally, it will be official, New York Knicks are the NBA Champions.” The ESPN personality warned that defending the title would be a much greater challenge. He said: “It will be a tough road ahead now, because you’ve got to defend that crown and I think the Oklahoma City Thunder are the favourites to win it all. “I don’t see anybody beating them all healthy in an NBA Finals.” It’s safe to say fans didn’t share his confidence and criticised his assessment of the Knicks. One replied, “The banner isn’t even up yet and he is already betraying the Knicks.” Another added: “Stop being so dramatic. We all know you will make sure to have fake emotion and espn all over it. Spike is more of a fan than you. You don’t even go to all the home games.”

item.title: ESPN's Shams Charania reveals major 76ers plan for LeBron James, Joel Embiid to start season
item.description: ESPN's Shams Charania reveals major 76ers plan for LeBron James, Joel Embiid to start season originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Coming into the season, the Philadelphia 76ers know they have plenty of players who can score the ball. Many believe the 76ers have what it takes to make a deep run in the playoffs. It is all about staying healthy, which is something LeBron James and Joel Embiid struggled with at times last season. This season, Embiid feels good as the regular season gets underway. “Pretty good," Embiid said. "Not bad. I don't know, that's probably (he took a pause), I said I would never dunk again. In the moment, he did block me the first time so I was kind of pissed off about it. So I was hoping that he would jump again, so that's why I went for it. But, yeah, that's probably the last dunk of my career." For James, there is a lot to monitor when it comes to his health. Despite the concerns, there is a strong belief that he looks much better now than he did at this point last season. “LeBron missed the first 15 games of last season and was clearly limited with his handle as he battled sciatica issues. It coincided with his first summer playing golf consistently. He looks noticeably healthier this offseason and more fluid with his movement,” NBA writer Damien Peters wrote. With both players dealing with injuries over the past year, Philadelphia has put a clear plan in place to manage their workloads. ESPN’s Shams Charania reported that the 76ers hope to limit both players to around 30 minutes per game during the first few weeks of the season. “My understanding is Lebron James, Joel Embiid - the hope is within the first few weeks of the season limit them to around 30 minutes a game,” Charania said. It is a smart approach by the organization, as Philadelphia looks to ensure that two of its key players are ready for the long season ahead. After all, the NBA regular season consists of 82 games, making it important for both stars to stay as healthy as possible. As the 76ers settle into the season, James and Embiid could see their minutes increase as they continue to build rhythm and get a feel for each game. For now, the plan is to keep both players around the 30-minute mark, barring situations such as overtime. Philadelphia will be looking to manage their workloads carefully and avoid putting unnecessary strain on its two stars. item.title: Fifa call out ‘concerted effort to undermine’ Gianni Infantino after apology from The Times
item.description: Fifa have acknowledged an apology from The Times over incorrect reporting that president Gianni Infantino was paid an undeclared second salary and have called out what it claims is a ‘concerted and ongoing effort’ to undermine the organisation and Infantino. An article published by The Times a week ago claimed that Infantino had received a second salary from Fifa and that he had failed to declare the payments with that information proving incorrect. The newspaper removed the incorrect information and issued an apology to both Fifa and Infantino over the report. Having seen and accepted the apology Fifa, via their Fifa Media account on X , took the opportunity to address the media and emphasise the need to ‘act responsibly’ and ‘carefully verify all sourcing’ in order to prevent false information from being published. The organisation’s statement also addressed what it perceives is a co-ordinated effort to undermine Infantino’s presidency after the 56-year-old came under scrutiny over a proposal to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors. That plan has raised concerns over his ability to perform in the role of president with Uefa among several parties to have called for his resignation. FIFA & FIFA PRESIDENT RECEIVES APOLOGY FROM ‘THE TIMES’ FIFA takes note of an apology published today by The Times following an inaccurate and damaging report: On 13 October 2026 (Sport), we reported that Gianni Infantino received a "second salary" from Fifa, which Fifa had… — FIFA Media (@fifamedia) October 20, 2026 Fifa’s statement reads: “FIFA takes note of an apology published today by The Times following an inaccurate and damaging report: ‘ “On 13 October 2026 (Sport), we reported that Gianni Infantino received a "second salary" from Fifa, which Fifa had failed to disclose. This is incorrect. There was no “second salary.” Regulations do not require Fifa to include expenses and reimbursements received by Mr Infantino in its annual report as they are not considered "compensation" under Swiss reporting requirements. We also accept Mr Infantino did not purchase a property in Miami at a suspected undervalue as we reported and neither he nor his family are the legal or beneficial owners of Shadi LLC and have no control over that company, as we suggested. We are happy to make these corrections and apologise to Mr Infantino and Fifa for the errors.’ “As FIFA stated in August, it is evident that there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine FIFA and its President. FIFA urges the media to act responsibly and carefully verify all sourcing to prevent the publication and subsequent reproduction of false and defamatory information. “FIFA welcomes legitimate scrutiny. But scrutiny is not a license to amplify false allegations. Where reporting is inaccurate, misleading, or totally false, as in this case, FIFA will continue to challenge it directly and vigorously.”

item.title: Rodri needed a rest for Barcelona ahead of Clasico, says Flick
item.description: Rodri was rested at kick-off for Barcelona's game against PSG on Tuesday (Ozan KOSE) Barcelona coach Hansi Flick said Rodri would be back in the starting line-up for Sunday's Clasico showdown against Real Madrid after being rested at kick-off in the Champions League loss away to Paris Saint-Germain. "Yes, but you know Rodri played a lot of minutes with the national team and also the last games with us," Flick told reporters after Barcelona's 4-2 defeat in Paris on Tuesday. "I spoke with him this morning and I told him that we made this decision, and Marc Bernal started instead. For me, it was a good solution what we did and hopefully he is fresh on Sunday." Rodri came on after an hour of the game in Paris, as Barcelona's perfect record this season came to an end. The Catalans had twice come from behind, with Xavi Espart and Lamine Yamal replying to goals by Desire Doue and Lucas Hernandez for the hosts. Yamal made it 2-2 in the 79th minute, but Vitinha put PSG back in front two minutes later before Fabian Ruiz sealed the victory for the defending European champions. "I think it was a fantastic game from both teams but we made too many mistakes, especially in possession," Flick said. "But I also saw a lot of good things. For me it was a great test for us and you also saw today what errors we have to improve to make things better. "We have to learn from this game. Today, in October, you cannot win titles. You win the Champions League in June." Flick added that the upcoming Clasico, in which Barca have the chance to go nine points ahead of Madrid in La Liga, influenced his team selection "a lot". - PSG injuries - Barcelona lost Dani Olmo to injury in the French capital, while the home team saw Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, two of their chief attacking stars, come off hurt. Dembele suffered a hamstring injury in the first half, and captain Marquinhos was also unable to finish the encounter. "I am not the doctor but the three players are injured which is the worst thing to come out of tonight's game," said PSG coach Luis Enrique. "Three injuries to three very important players. It is the worst news we could have had, but that is what happens in football." PSG have won their first three games in this season's league phase, scoring 14 goals in the process, as they aim to win the Champions League for the third year running. They are therefore comfortably on course to reach the knockout phase, although their coach is not getting carried away. The top eight teams in the league phase go straight through to the last 16. "We have already played against our two opponents from Pot A," he said, with this win following a 4-2 triumph at Manchester City last week. "But I will remind you that last year we also won our first three games and we did not finish in the top eight. "We will enjoy this but then we will start to think about this weekend's game against Lyon." as/mw

Mac Allister obliged. “The character, when you are 2-0 down and not playing well, he doesn’t panic,” noted Iraola. Mac Allister was aided by the excellent Rio Ngumoha while Ronald Araujo’s equaliser again underlined what a fine bit of business Liverpool did by borrowing the Uruguayan from Barcelona . His footballing intelligence gives him an eye for goal. “I'm not tall but I love going in the box,” said the Argentinian. “My dad is a bit smaller than me but he was quite good in the air so maybe it's something I got from him.” So the younger Mac Allister rose highest to glance in a header from Kostas Tsimikas’ corner. His second showed another attribute for a goalscoring midfielder. “He can arrive inside the box like a No 8,” added Iraola. Mac Allister timed his run into the penalty box perfectly to put Liverpool ahead, crashing in a shot from six yards off the underside of the bar and following a cutback from Ngumoha. “It’s up there with one of the best I’ve played,” said the 18-year-old, who became the youngest player since Michael Owen to make two goals in a game for Liverpool. The first came when Araujo snuck in at the far post to capitalise on poor defending by Cardona and head in the teenager’s cross. It was, albeit indirectly, a second goal from a corner and a second in as many Champions League games for Araujo. ‘Big Ron’ is proving a big threat from set-pieces. After Mac Allister doubled his tally for the night, Wirtz drove in Liverpool’s fourth following a pass from Cody Gakpo , who was making his first appearance for a month. item.description: PARSIPPANY — Ian Johnson had already been doing plenty of running around before the gun even went off to start the Morris County cross country championships. Lakers assistant coach Brandon Chen told him to take a few deep breaths and try to forget about the drama. Johnson had renewed motivation, if only to keep Allison from reminding him about the mistake. EL SEGUNDO, Calif. — Walker Kessler expects some nerves before he takes the floor for his first regular-season game with the Los Angeles Lakers. He also expects basketball to take over once the game begins. Speaking after Tuesday’s practice, Kessler described his anticipation ahead of Wednesday’s season opener against the Golden State Warriors. After working through training camp and getting preseason minutes alongside his new teammates, the center is ready to begin learning through games that count. “I think there’s gonna be a lot of nerves going into the game,” Kessler said. “But as soon as the whistle blows,” he expects the rest to take care of itself. For Kessler, the opener represents a return to regular-season competition and the beginning of his place in an organization with a lot of expectations. He expressed gratitude for the opportunity while keeping his attention on what he can control: improving each day and helping L.A. win. Communication comes first against Golden State The Warriors present an immediate test of the defensive communication Kessler has been working to develop. Golden State’s movement requires defenders to follow more than the ball. Off-ball screens can create openings before a possession reaches its final action, putting pressure on teammates to communicate assignments and react together. Kessler pointed to that movement when discussing the matchup. Although the teams saw each other during the preseason, he acknowledged that some players were unavailable for those meetings. His approach to becoming more vocal is rooted in repetition. “I think it’s repetition, building a habit of overcommunicating on every possession,” Kessler said. Jared Young, Mark Vientos, Brett Baty, Eric Wagaman, Christopher Morel and Jorge Polanco all saw time at first base this season, but no one really stood out as a long-term solution. This offseason, David Stearns will be tasked with fixing his mistake and finding a reliable first baseman. One option for the Mets could be longtime rival infielder Alec Bohm. Bohm moved to first base this year when the Philadelphia Phillies acquired Luis Arraez at the trade deadline. Arraez played second base, Bryson Stott moved to third base, Bryce Harper moved to right field and Bohm moved to first base. Bohm was not a great defender at first base, but he was better than he was at third base. He was an All-Star in 2024, but his offense has declined since then. In 2024, Bohm had a .280/.332/.448 slash line with 15 home runs. His slash line in the last two seasons was .266/.322/.395, but he ended this season on a high note, perhaps giving himself some more allure in free agency. If the Mets think he can maintain the production he had in the second half, then he could be a great addition. item.description: Phil Foden shouted the loudest on a quiet night at the Etihad Stadium, announcing his personal return to form with an instinctive hat-trick as Manchester City dispatched AEK Athens with little fuss. Enzo Maresca had called for City to make their own noise amid the cacophony around the club but a businesslike victory in front of 20,000 fewer than watched the weekend’s win over Ipswich was required to get their Champions League back on track after suffering at the hands of Paris Saint-Germain . Those in attendance, officially 40,042 but that felt optimistic, saw Foden shine on the right wing and as a central striker, showing there is life without Erling Haaland, who watched from the bench. Admittedly, the opposition were not a match for the Premier League side, whose other goals came from Elliot Anderson and Rayan Cherki. Stavros Pilios’s consolation was more a reward for the boisterous fans in yellow and black, who created the atmosphere, than for the overall efforts of the visitors. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Kulusevski and Maddison return to form but are Tottenham also back?
item.description: As Tottenham edged to victory over Coventry , a familiar face among the post-match salutations. Could that be Dejan Kulusevski? For it was he, playing 526 days since his last Spurs appearance. Much has changed though still much stays the same. Ben Davies’s deflected late clincher catapulted Spurs up to … 16th. When Kulusevski last played on 11 May 2025, Tottenham were 17th, the position in which they finished both that season and in 2025-26. Further to Peters and Lee [ Monday’s Football Daily letters] another 70s example that occurred to me was the West Ham players Mervyn Day and Bill Green . They were both in the West Ham United team from 1976-78, and in Carlisle United’s greatest season 1974-75. When Green was still at Carlisle, he played against West Ham’s Day. So plenty of Green Day commentary opportunities there. Of course, the band hadn’t formed yet, but who knows, perhaps they thought of the band’s name whilst watching some old 70s football footage” – Bob Dunning. On the subject of musical football matchups, all I can say is that it’s just a shame Gareth Barry was at Manchester City a few years too late to play alongside David White ” – Tim Russell. As an aside to the music makers and fitba’, in the late 60s at the old Highbury, we would be entertained at every first team match by the local constabulary brass band. Such was the style of play, it did introduce a some element of entertainment into our visits to the old stadium” – Tommy Boyd (and, surprisingly, others). item.title: Uefa demands Fifa releases documents relating to World Cup sell-off scheme
item.description: European governing body gives two-week deadline Letter addresses other issues including Balogun affair Uefa has given Fifa a two-week deadline to release key documents relating to Gianni Infantino’s World Cup sell-off plan and other governance issues in its latest critique of football’s world governing body . A letter sent to Fifa’s general secretary, Mattias Grafström, by his counterpart at Uefa, Theodore Theodoridis, is accompanied by an eight-page document that has more than 50 questions about Fifa’s handling of dozens of issues over the past 12 months. These include the proposed sale of 20% of its commercial rights, the Folarin Balogun affair , the peace prize and relations with Donald Trump and the arrangements for next year’s Fifa presidential election. Uefa’s document also makes a number of allegations about potential conflicts of interests at Fifa, as well as repeating calls for a “genuinely independent” governance review. Continue reading...

His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. Savage has long been a joker figure – an image born in his playing days, when he hurtled around midfield with long blond hair bouncing, launching into challenges that at one point made him the most booked player in Premier League history. A pantomime villain, a prankster and an eccentric who was once fined £10,000 by the Football Association – and two weeks’ wages by Leicester – for using the referee Graham Poll’s toilet before a match. (Savage blamed an upset stomach brought on by antibiotics). Continue reading...

item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. item.title: Mikel Arteta’s new contract reflects where the power now lies at Arsenal | Ed Aarons
item.description: From transfers to stadium works and even the training-ground dog, there is no doubting the Spaniard’s influence at the club If anyone doubts Mikel Arteta’s status as No 1 at Arsenal in the week he committed his future to the club until 2030 , just ask Win the dog. The chocolate labrador who played a starring role in the celebrations when Arsenal were crowned Premier League champions in May has become part of the family at the training ground in Hertfordshire since being introduced by Arteta in May 2023. Kai Havertz, David Raya and Mikel Merino, who issues commands in Spanish and has spoken about spending time with Win when out for three months with a foot injury, are particular favourites. But, according to sources close to Win, a therapy dog trained not to bark, there is no contest when it comes to her preferred human: Arteta. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
